cs.t: I've gone a bit neo-retro on this one. I have a Raspberry Pi Pico on a Pico Explorer (from Pimoroni), to revisit more modern versions of the type of electronic projects I used to do in my youth. Look those up if you haven't seen/heard of them yet. Both products are brand new on the market. I have a few old dips, like 555 timers, a 595 shift register, and an optocoupler, and now on the market for some "typical" logic gates. Eventually I'll find a good "grab bag" of different logic chips, like the 7400N (which has 4 AND gates). The addition of a microcontroller like the Pico allows you to do a lot more interesting things than simple LED flip-flopping to see results, and it has a screen for more intelligent and functional visuals. I find it really interesting to "talk" to the chips through the Pico, which I think is a pretty ideal way to cement the functionality quite clearly in mind. I might make a few mini projects and post them online this summer.
